``` {r echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(scales)

# Load dataset
Global_Development_Indicators <- read_csv("R-DATA/project_1_Global_Development_Indicators.csv")

# Country metadata from the World Bank: real economies have a Region, aggregates do not
country_meta <- read_csv("R-DATA/country_metadata.csv") %>%
  select(`Country Code`, Region, IncomeGroup)

real_countries <- country_meta %>%
  filter(!is.na(Region))

# Clean data: convert ".." to NA and numeric conversion
base_clean <- Global_Development_Indicators %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("19") | starts_with("20"), ~ifelse(.x == "..", NA, as.numeric(.x))))

# Extract and reshape indicators
gdp_data <- base_clean %>%
  filter(`Series Name` == "GDP (current US$)") %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Country Code`, starts_with("20")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("20"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "GDP_total") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "\\d{4}"))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_total))

pop_data <- base_clean %>%
  filter(`Series Name` == "Population, total") %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Country Code`, starts_with("20")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("20"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Population") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "\\d{4}"))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Population))

internet_data <- base_clean %>%
  filter(`Series Name` == "Individuals using the Internet (% of population)") %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Country Code`, starts_with("20")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("20"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Internet_users_pct") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "\\d{4}"))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Internet_users_pct))

education_data <- base_clean %>%
  filter(`Series Name` == "Adolescents out of school (% of lower secondary school age)") %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Country Code`, starts_with("20")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("20"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Out_of_school_pct") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "\\d{4}"))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Out_of_school_pct))

# Combine datasets before any country filtering
combined <- gdp_data %>%
  left_join(pop_data, by = c("Country Name", "Country Code", "Year")) %>%
  mutate(GDP_per_capita = GDP_total / Population) %>%
  left_join(internet_data, by = c("Country Name", "Country Code", "Year")) %>%
  left_join(education_data, by = c("Country Name", "Country Code", "Year")) %>%
  filter(Year >= 2000)

# Keep only real economies by joining on country code (replaces the old name-based filter)
analysis_data <- combined %>%
  inner_join(real_countries, by = "Country Code") %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Country Code`, Region, IncomeGroup, Year,
         GDP_per_capita, Internet_users_pct, Out_of_school_pct)

complete_countries <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita), !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  distinct(`Country Name`)

glimpse(analysis_data)
```

# Introduction

This project explores global development indicators from 2000 onwards.\
We are particularly interested in understanding the relationship between economic development, digital access, and education across countries.

The main objectives of this analysis are:

-   Examine trends in GDP per capita and internet usage over time.
-   Understand how economic prosperity correlates with digital connectivity.
-   Identify countries that deviate from expected patterns, highlighting potential development gaps.
-   Provide insights into the evolution of key development indicators over the last two decades.

## Data Cleaning and Preparation

The dataset was obtained from the World Bank Global Development Indicators service.

**Steps undertaken for data preparation:**

-   Converted all non-numeric entries to `NA` and converted years to numeric format.

-   Filtered for the indicators of interest: GDP, population, internet usage, and adolescents out of school.

-   Calculated GDP per capita using GDP and population data.

-   Filtered to include data from the year 2000 onward.

-   Excluded aggregates (e.g., World, East Asia & Pacific, OECD members) by keeping only economies that have a region in the World Bank country metadata, joined on country code.

**Outcome:**

-   The final dataset covers `r n_distinct(analysis_data[["Country Code"]])` countries from `r min(analysis_data$Year)` to `r max(analysis_data$Year)` (`r nrow(analysis_data)` country-years).

-   `r n_distinct(complete_countries[["Country Name"]])` countries have both GDP per capita and internet usage for at least one year.

-   GDP per capita is available for `r round(mean(!is.na(analysis_data$GDP_per_capita)) * 100, 1)`% of country-years and internet usage for `r round(mean(!is.na(analysis_data$Internet_users_pct)) * 100, 1)`%. Out-of-school data is far sparser (`r round(mean(!is.na(analysis_data$Out_of_school_pct)) * 100, 1)`%), so it is only used in the final check in section 4.

## Data Quality Check: Country Filter

An earlier version of this analysis removed aggregates by matching words in country names. This check compares that approach with the metadata join used above.

```{r}
old_pattern <- "World|income|Arab|East Asia|Europe|Latin|Middle|North America|South Asia|Sub-Saharan"

old_filter_names <- combined %>%
  filter(!str_detect(`Country Name`, old_pattern)) %>%
  distinct(`Country Name`) %>%
  pull()

new_filter_names <- analysis_data %>%
  distinct(`Country Name`) %>%
  pull()

wrongly_removed <- setdiff(new_filter_names, old_filter_names)
wrongly_kept <- setdiff(old_filter_names, new_filter_names)

cat("Real countries the name filter removed:", length(wrongly_removed), "\n")
print(wrongly_removed)

cat("\nKept by the name filter but not in the World Bank country list:", length(wrongly_kept), "\n")
print(wrongly_kept)
```

**Insight:** Matching on names is fragile: "Arab" also matches the United Arab Emirates. Joining on the World Bank's country codes removes aggregates without dropping real countries.

# Exploratory Data Analysis

### 3.1 Summary Statistics

```{r}
# Summary statistics for key variables
summary_stats <- analysis_data %>%
  select(GDP_per_capita, Internet_users_pct) %>%
  summary()

print("Summary Statistics:")
print(summary_stats)

# More detailed statistics
detailed_stats <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita) | !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  summarise(
    # GDP per capita statistics
    GDP_mean = mean(GDP_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
    GDP_median = median(GDP_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
    GDP_sd = sd(GDP_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
    GDP_min = min(GDP_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
    GDP_max = max(GDP_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Internet usage statistics
    Internet_mean = mean(Internet_users_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Internet_median = median(Internet_users_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Internet_sd = sd(Internet_users_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Internet_min = min(Internet_users_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Internet_max = max(Internet_users_pct, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Data availability
    total_observations = n(),
    gdp_available = sum(!is.na(GDP_per_capita)),
    internet_available = sum(!is.na(Internet_users_pct)),
    both_available = sum(!is.na(GDP_per_capita) & !is.na(Internet_users_pct))
  )

print("Detailed Statistics:")
print(detailed_stats)
```

**Insight:** GDP per capita is skewed with a few very high-income countries. Internet usage shows a wide spread with gradual global adoption.

### 3.2 Data Availability by Year

```{r}
# Check data availability by year
data_by_year <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    countries = n_distinct(`Country Name`),
    gdp_available = sum(!is.na(GDP_per_capita)),
    internet_available = sum(!is.na(Internet_users_pct)),
    both_available = sum(!is.na(GDP_per_capita) & !is.na(Internet_users_pct)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print("Data Availability by Year:")
print(data_by_year)
```

**Insight:** Data availability improves after 2005, allowing reliable comparisons across countries.

### 3.3 Correlation Analysis

```{r}
correlation <- cor(analysis_data$GDP_per_capita, analysis_data$Internet_users_pct,
                   use = "complete.obs")

log_set <- analysis_data %>% filter(GDP_per_capita > 0)
correlation_log <- cor(log(log_set$GDP_per_capita), log_set$Internet_users_pct,
                       use = "complete.obs")

cat("Correlation between GDP per capita and Internet usage:", round(correlation, 3), "\n")
cat("Correlation between log GDP per capita and Internet usage:", round(correlation_log, 3), "\n")
```

**Insight:** The correlation is `r round(correlation, 3)` on raw GDP per capita and `r round(correlation_log, 3)` on log GDP per capita. The log version matches the log-scale charts below, so it better describes the relationship they show.

### 3.4 Visualizations

#### 3.4.1 GDP per Capita Distribution

```{r}
gdp_histogram <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = GDP_per_capita)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of GDP per Capita",
    subtitle = "Log scale, all countries and years",
    x = "GDP per Capita (USD, log scale)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(gdp_histogram)
```

**Insight:** Most countries cluster at lower GDP levels; a few countries are extreme high-income outliers.

#### 3.4.2 Internet Usage Distribution

```{r}
 internet_histogram <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Internet_users_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Internet Usage",
    subtitle = "Percentage of population using internet",
    x = "Internet Users (% of population)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(internet_histogram)

```

**Insight:** Internet usage varies widely; adoption has increased over time, especially in developing countries.

#### 3.4.3 GDP vs Internet Usage Scatter Plot

```{r}
scatter_plot <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita), !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = GDP_per_capita, y = Internet_users_pct)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Economic Development vs Digital Access",
    subtitle = paste("Correlation (log GDP):", round(correlation_log, 3)),
    x = "GDP per Capita (USD, log scale)",
    y = "Internet Users (% of population)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(scatter_plot)
```

**Insight:** Positive trend confirms richer countries generally have higher internet penetration, with some notable outliers.

#### 3.4.4 Time Series Analysis of Global Internet Usage

```{r}
time_series <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita), !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_gdp = mean(GDP_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_internet = mean(Internet_users_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    countries = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_internet), color = "forestgreen", size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = avg_internet), color = "forestgreen", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Global Average Internet Usage Over Time",
    subtitle = "Average across all countries with available data",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Internet Users (% of population)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(time_series)

```

**Insight:** Internet usage has steadily increased globally, reflecting digital adoption trends across nations.

#### 3.4.5 Internet Access by World Bank Income Group

```{r}
income_levels <- c("Low income", "Lower middle income", "Upper middle income", "High income")

box_plot <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Internet_users_pct), IncomeGroup %in% income_levels) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(IncomeGroup, levels = income_levels),
             y = Internet_users_pct)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = IncomeGroup), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_brewer(type = "seq", palette = "Blues") +
  labs(
    title = "Internet Access by Income Group",
    subtitle = "World Bank income classification (current), all years",
    x = "World Bank Income Group",
    y = "Internet Users (% of population)",
    fill = "Income Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(box_plot)

```

**Insight:** Higher income groups consistently have higher internet usage; some low-income countries outperform expectations. Income groups are the World Bank's current classification, applied to every year.

#### 3.5 Outlier Analysis

```{r}
outliers_high_gdp_low_internet <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita), !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  filter(GDP_per_capita > 20000, Internet_users_pct < 50) %>%
  arrange(desc(GDP_per_capita)) %>%
  select(`Country Name`, Year, GDP_per_capita, Internet_users_pct)

if(nrow(outliers_high_gdp_low_internet) > 0) {
  print("Countries with High GDP but Low Internet Usage:")
  print(outliers_high_gdp_low_internet)
}

# Low GDP but high internet usage
outliers_low_gdp_high_internet <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(GDP_per_capita), !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  filter(GDP_per_capita < 5000, Internet_users_pct > 50) %>%
  arrange(desc(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  select(`Country Name`, Year, GDP_per_capita, Internet_users_pct)

if(nrow(outliers_low_gdp_high_internet) > 0) {
  print("Countries with Low GDP but High Internet Usage:")
  print(outliers_low_gdp_high_internet)
}


```

**Insight:** Outliers suggest countries with unique economic or technological circumstances; these may be of interest for further study. Thresholds are in current US dollars, so they are not adjusted for inflation.

#### 3.6 Recent Trends (2020-2023)

```{r}
recent_trends <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(Year >= 2020, !is.na(GDP_per_capita), !is.na(Internet_users_pct)) %>%
  group_by(`Country Name`) %>%
  summarise(
    years_available = n(),
    avg_gdp = mean(GDP_per_capita),
    avg_internet = mean(Internet_users_pct),
    latest_year = max(Year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(years_available >= 2) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_internet))

print("Recent Trends (2020-2023) - Top 10 Countries by Internet Usage:")
print(head(recent_trends, 10))
```

**Insight:** High internet usage countries continue to lead, while many developing nations show rapid improvements since 2020.

#### 3.7 Key Insights Summary

```{r}
cat("\n=== KEY INSIGHTS FROM EXPLORATORY ANALYSIS ===\n")
cat("1. Data Coverage:", nrow(analysis_data), "total observations\n")
cat("2. GDP-Internet Correlation:", round(correlation, 3), "(log GDP:", round(correlation_log, 3), ")\n")
cat("3. Countries with complete data:", nrow(complete_countries), "\n")
cat("4. Year range:", min(analysis_data$Year), "to", max(analysis_data$Year), "\n")
cat("5. Average global internet usage has", ifelse(correlation > 0.5, "strong", "moderate"), "correlation with economic development\n")

```

**Summary:**

-   Economic development strongly correlates with digital access.

-   Global internet adoption is steadily increasing.

-   Outliers and trends provide insight into countries that perform above or below expectations.

#### 3.8 Internet Usage and Adolescents Out of School

```{r}
education_check <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Internet_users_pct), !is.na(Out_of_school_pct))

education_cor <- cor(education_check$Internet_users_pct, education_check$Out_of_school_pct)

cat("Country-years with both values:", nrow(education_check), "\n")
cat("Countries:", n_distinct(education_check$`Country Name`), "\n")
cat("Correlation between internet usage and out-of-school rate:", round(education_cor, 3), "\n")
```

# Key Insights and Implications

1.  **Economic and Digital Development:** Wealthier countries generally have better internet access, confirming the strong correlation between GDP per capita and digital infrastructure.

2.  **Global Trends:** Internet adoption has increased globally, with notable improvements in developing regions over the last decade.

3.  **Outliers:** Some countries deviate from expected patterns, providing opportunities for targeted policy interventions or further research.

4.  **Education and Development:** Across `r nrow(education_check)` country-years with both values, the correlation between internet usage and the share of adolescents out of school is `r round(education_cor, 3)`. Out-of-school data is sparse, so this is indicative only.

**Limitations:**

-   Missing data for some countries, especially in early years, may bias trends.

-   Indicators are national averages and may mask regional disparities.

-   GDP is in current US dollars, so comparisons over time are not inflation-adjusted.

-   Averages weight every country equally, regardless of population.

**Future Research:**

-   Examine subnational data to capture regional inequalities.

-   Explore causal relationships between GDP growth and digital adoption.

-   Investigate other indicators such as life expectancy, literacy, or healthcare access in conjunction with digital access.
